chain.label: A300-600 rudder control system highly sensitive at high airspeed
chain.trigger: the A300-600 rudder control system couples a rudder travel limiter system that increases in sensitivity with airspeed... with the lightest pedal forces of all the transport-category aircraft evaluated

chain.label: American Airlines AAMP training encouraged rudder for roll control and portrayed unrealistic wake upsets
chain.trigger: the American Airlines AAMP ground school training encouraged pilots to use rudder to assist with roll control during recovery from upsets, including wake turbulence

chain.label: Pilots not trained on restricted rudder pedal travel or airplane response to large rudder inputs at high speed
chain.trigger: before the flight 587 accident, pilots were not being adequately trained on what effect rudder pedal inputs have on the Airbus A300-600 at high airspeeds and how the airplane's rudder travel limiter system operates

caused_by.evidence: American Airlines did not teach its pilots during training that rudder pedal movement would become restricted as airspeed increased

chain.label: First officer's predisposition to overreact to wake turbulence
chain.trigger: the first officer had a tendency to overreact to wake turbulence by taking unnecessary actions, including making excessive control inputs

caused_by.evidence: the AAMP excessive bank angle simulator exercise could have caused the first officer to have an unrealistic and exaggerated view of the effects of wake turbulence

chain.label: Second wake vortex encounter from preceding Japan Air Lines 747
chain.trigger: about 0915:51, the load factors began excursions... The airplane performance study found that these excursions were also consistent with a wake turbulence encounter

chain.label: First officer's excessive initial control wheel and right rudder pedal input
chain.trigger: the first officer's initial control wheel input in response to the second wake turbulence encounter was too aggressive, and his initial rudder pedal input response was unnecessary to control the airplane

caused_by.evidence: the rudder pedals moved to 1.7 inches right at 0915:51.9
the initial rudder pedal input in response to the second wake turbulence encounter was consistent with the first officer's tendencies to overreact

the first officer may have been concerned that the airplane was about to enter a hazardous bank angle upset and, therefore, responded with both the control wheel and rudder pedal as he had been encouraged to do in the simulator
the full rudder deflection that he achieved may have been the result of his lack of knowledge concerning the pedal restrictions or the sensitivity of the rudder control system

chain.label: First officer misattributed the airplane's yaw/roll response to the wake rather than his own inputs
chain.trigger: the first officer likely did not recognize that the airplane's motion was being caused by his control inputs rather than the wake turbulence

caused_by.evidence: the large right yaw and subsequent rolling moment resulting from the first officer's initial rudder pedal input were surprising and confusing to him
the first officer may have perceived that he was only using about 30 percent of the rudder authority, making it harder for him to associate the airplane motion with his pedal inputs

chain.label: Sustained alternating full rudder pedal reversals (adverse aircraft-pilot coupling)
chain.trigger: the rudder pedals moved from 1.7 inches right to 1.7 inches left, 1.7 inches right, 2.0 inches right, 2.4 inches left, and 1.3 inches right between 0915:52 and 0915:58.5

caused_by.evidence: the sudden acceleration to the right may have led him to believe that the wake was acting to roll the airplane to the right... prompted a full and immediate application of control wheel and rudder pedal to the left
the small pedal displacements of the A300-600 rudder control system at 240 knots may have facilitated the first officer's large, rapid inputs to the rudder system

chain.label: Sideslip angle buildup produced aerodynamic loads about twice limit load on vertical stabilizer
chain.trigger: the first officer's cyclic rudder pedal inputs... led to increasing sideslip angles that, along with the continued rudder deflections, produced extremely high aerodynamic loads on the vertical stabilizer

caused_by.evidence: the aerodynamic loads on the vertical stabilizer were about two times the loads defined by the limit load design envelope

chain.label: Right rear main attachment lug fractured and vertical stabilizer separated in flight
chain.trigger: the vertical stabilizer's right rear main attachment fitting fractured at 0915:58.4, and the vertical stabilizer separated from the airplane immediately afterward

caused_by.evidence: The vertical stabilizer fractured from the fuselage in overstress, starting with the right rear lug while the vertical stabilizer was exposed to aerodynamic loads that were about twice the certified limit load design envelope

chain.label: Loss of directional control and uncontrolled descent after stabilizer loss
chain.trigger: the sideslip angle continued to increase and reached 31º at the end of the FDR recording... 'what the hell are we into…we're stuck in it'

caused_by.evidence: An airplane cannot be flown without its vertical stabilizer

chain.label: Both engines separated in flight during uncontrolled descent
chain.trigger: The airplane's engines subsequently separated in flight and were found several blocks north and east of the main wreckage site

caused_by.evidence: engine separation occurred during the out-of-control airplane motion that followed the separation of the vertical stabilizer

chain.label: Airplane crashed into Belle Harbor residential area and burned
chain.trigger: crashed into a residential area of Belle Harbor, New York... the airplane was destroyed by impact forces and a postcrash fire

caused_by.evidence: the airplane appeared to be intact when it impacted the ground at an 85º to a 90º angle
In the immediate vicinity of the impact area, four homes were destroyed

chain.label: 260 aboard and 5 on the ground killed
chain.trigger: All 260 people aboard the airplane and 5 people on the ground were killed

caused_by.evidence: The accident was not survivable for any of the airplane occupants
